C O M P A N I O N D O C U M E N T — M A S T E R A S T R O L O G I C A L C O M P E N D I U M
APRIL
Complete Illustration
Reference Guide
Sixteen Pen-and-Ink Illustrations in the Style of Brett Helquist
Full Art Direction, Technical Specifications & AI Generation Prompts
Born: September 6, 1990 • Geneva, NY • Sun in Virgo • Moon in Aries •
Sagittarius Rising
Prepared June 2026 • For the Commissioned Illustrator • Confidential
This document is the complete illustration brief for the sixteen pen-and-ink
works commissioned to accompany April: The Complete Master Astrological
Compendium. It is addressed directly to the illustrator and contains everything
needed to execute the full sequence: style specifications, compositional
direction, technical crosshatch notes, placement instructions, and AI-generation
prompts for reference imagery. Read the Style Guide in full before beginning
any individual illustration. The illustrations form a unified visual language across
the document — each one should feel as though it belongs to the same hand,
the same world, the same ongoing story.
BRETT HELQUIST STYLE GUIDE

Technical Specifications for the Illustrator
✦ ✦ ✦
PARAGRAPH I — LINE QUALITY AND TECHNIQUE
Brett Helquist's signature technique is built on extraordinarily dense crosshatching —
parallel lines layered at multiple angles to create deep, velvety shadows that give his
illustrations the quality of antique engravings. The linework is always confident, never
sketchy; each mark is deliberate. Crosshatch density determines the depth of shadow
— the darkest areas (deep corners, heavy fabrics, the underside of a face) may have
four or five layers of perpendicular hatching, while highlighted areas are achieved
simply through leaving white space rather than adding marks. The pen line itself is
variable weight: slightly heavier on defining edges (silhouette, facial features, object
contours), finer for interior texture detail. In practice, this means approaching each
illustration in layers — establish the composition and silhouettes first with confident
contour lines, then build shadow density inward from the darkest points outward,
allowing the crosshatch to thin organically rather than stopping artificially. The line
never wavers. The line always knows where it is going.
PARAGRAPH II — ATMOSPHERE AND LIGHTING
Helquist's illustrations are always lit from a single, specific source — a candle, a
window, a doorway, a star. The light source is always dramatically directional,
creating high contrast between lit and shadowed areas. Faces are typically lit from
slightly below or from one side, giving them a cinematic quality. Backgrounds are
often dark, pushing the figure into relief. He frequently uses a vignette technique —
darkening the corners of the image while keeping the center luminous — that creates
an almost spotlight effect on the central figure or object. Compositions are
intentionally theatrical. In this series, each illustration's light source is specified
explicitly in its technical brief; adhere to that specification as a primary architectural
decision. The light source is not merely an aesthetic choice — in each case it carries
symbolic meaning. The warm amber of candle and stage footlight belongs to the past;
the cool silver of stars and moonlight belongs to the present; the golden-white of the
dawn horizon belongs to the future.

PARAGRAPH III — CHARACTER DESIGN AND FACIAL EXPRESSION
Helquist's human figures are expressive in a controlled, literary way — the face
always communicates something specific: determination, sorrow, wonder, resolve —
never generic contentment. His characters have a slight elongation, a refinement that
reads as slightly older and more serious than their literal age. For April specifically,
she should be rendered as a woman in her mid-thirties: clear-eyed, precise in bearing,
dark hair, slightly serious in expression but with warmth present. She should never
look defeated or small — even in scenes of weight or difficulty, her posture and
expression should carry the quality of someone who is working with something rather
than being crushed by it. Her Sagittarius Rising should be visible in her bearing —
there is a quality of the explorer or the archer about her even in stillness. When her
face is visible, the viewer should feel they are looking at someone who has already
survived a great deal and is not afraid of more. When her face is not visible — when
she is shown from behind, as in the cover and final illustrations — her posture alone
must carry this quality. Posture is character.
PARAGRAPH IV — COLOR, TONE, AND THE TWO-COLOR
TREATMENT
The base illustrations should be executed in black ink on white paper with rich
greyscale values achieved through crosshatching density. However, a selective two-
color treatment is strongly recommended for the final printed document: black ink as
the primary, with a single accent color — antique gold (Pantone 871 or equivalent; see
Production Notes) — applied selectively to the following elements: the Galactic
Center's glow and spiral in the cover image and wherever it reappears; candle flames
in all ritual and intimate illustrations; star light, fixed star labels, and the Galactic
Center wherever it appears; decorative borders and ornamental elements; any
astrological symbols, sigils, or glyphs used as centerpieces. This creates the visual
language of an illuminated manuscript — ink on vellum, touched with gold — which
perfectly suits the document's subject matter and honors both its scholarly rigor and
its sacred intention. The gold should never be used so broadly that it loses its
selective power. When in doubt, use less. The gold marks the places in the image
where something holy or significant lives.

THE SIXTEEN ILLUSTRATIONS
Complete Art Direction Briefs
Each illustration is presented below in full. The format for each entry is
consistent: metadata, purpose, mood, light source, technical notes, full art
direction prompt, alternate simplified version, and AI generation prompt. Read
each entry in its entirety before beginning that illustration. The entries are
presented in numbering order, not in document order — refer to the Document
Placement Map for production sequencing.
Illustration 01 of 16
The Threshold Between Worlds
Document Location: Cover Page — April: The Complete Master Astrological
Compendium
Page Position: Full bleed cover illustration; figure centered in lower two-thirds; title text to
occupy upper third
Dimensions: 7″ × 9″ (full page)
P U R P O S E I N D O C U M E N T
Establishes the entire document's visual and emotional register; immediately
communicates the scale and depth of April's chart; the viewer should feel they are
entering something significant.
M O O D
Vast — Luminous — Slightly Sacred — Ready
L I G H T S O U R C E
The Galactic Center ahead — a spiral of light on the horizon, warmer than starlight, more
cosmic than solar; the sole and total source of illumination in the image.

T E C H N I C A L N O T E S
This is the most complex illustration in the set. The sky should have the highest density of
fine crosshatch stippling — thousands of individual stars rendered as tiny variations in
white space. The figure should be in near-full silhouette from behind, with only the hands
and the back of the head rendered in detail. The Galactic Center spiral should be the one
area where the gold accent color appears most prominently — rendered in gold ink, fine
spiraling lines radiating outward. The vignette darkening of all four corners is essential.
This is the image the reader sees before they read a single word; it must earn everything
that follows.
F U L L A R T D I R E C T I O N P R O M P T
A young woman stands at the precise edge of a vast stone threshold
—
the archway framed by crumbling gothic stonework dripping with ivy, carved with
zodiac symbols and planetary glyphs barely visible in the shadow. Her back is to the
viewer; she faces an immense night sky where the Galactic Center blazes at the
horizon as a luminous, swirling spiral
—
brighter than any star, more structured than a nebula, clearly a source of directed
light. Her posture is composed, one hand resting on the stone archway, the other at
her side. The constellations of Sagittarius (her Ascendant), Virgo (her Sun), and
Aries (her Moon) form visible outlines in the densely crosshatched starfield above.
Carved into the stone floor beneath her feet: an archer's arrow pointing forward, a
full moon circle, a wheel with twelve divisions. The figure's clothing suggests layers
—
a long coat, boots
—

appropriate for a long journey. The stone archway has the patina of great age, the
ivy the suggestion of things long preserved. The total impression: she is standing at
the threshold of something enormous, and she is walking through, not hesitating.
A L T E R N A T E / S I M P L I F I E D V E R S I O N
Figure in silhouette at a simple arched doorway, galactic spiral visible ahead, constellation
outlines faint in sky above. Stone floor with astrological glyph (the Ascendant symbol).
A I G E N E R A T I O N P R O M P T ( M I D J O U R N E Y / D A L L - E C O M P A T I B L E )
A young woman seen from behind, standing in a gothic stone archway at night,
facing a vast starfield where the galactic center glows as a luminous spiral on the
horizon, intricate crosshatch pen and ink illustration, dense Victorian etching style,
ivy-covered stone ruins, zodiac symbols carved in stone floor, Virgo Sagittarius and
Aries constellations visible, dramatic chiaroscuro lighting from the galactic center,
antique illustration aesthetic, black and white with gold accent, hyper-detailed
linework, A Series of Unfortunate Events illustration style --ar 7:9 --style raw
Illustration 02 of 16
The Karmic Axis — Past Lives
Document Location: Section 1: Past Lives & Karmic Inheritance — placed after the opening
two paragraphs, before the South Node analysis
Page Position: Half-page, full width, centered
Dimensions: 6″ × 4″
P U R P O S E I N D O C U M E N T

Visualizes the karmic axis of South Node Leo H7 (the past) and North Node Aquarius H1
(the future) — the foundational karmic architecture of the entire chart.
M O O D
Theatrical — Melancholy — Turning
L I G H T S O U R C E
Split — warm amber footlights from stage left (South Node/past); cool starlight from the
open doorway on stage right (North Node/future).
T E C H N I C A L N O T E S
The split lighting is this illustration's most important technical element. The left half of the
image (stage, performance, crowd) uses warm tones achieved through lighter
crosshatching and white highlights; the right half (the open doorway, the stars) uses
denser crosshatching with fine white dots for stars. The figure herself should be lit from
the right — she is already turning toward the North Node.
F U L L A R T D I R E C T I O N P R O M P T
A Victorian performance stage, richly dressed. Center stage: a woman in theatrical
Leo costume
—
a dress with a lion's mane collar and small crown, akin to an operatic queen
—
but her face is turned away from the crowd below. On the left: a vast theater
audience in shadow, hands raised in adoration. Ghostly translucent figures float
around the performer
—
past-life echoes: a Roman senator, a medieval bishop, a Victorian socialite
—

all wearing the woman's face in slightly different form, the soul across multiple
lifetimes. On the right side of the stage: a heavy velvet curtain is drawn back slightly,
and through the gap a doorway opens into a night sky filled with the constellation
Aquarius. Cold starlight spills through the gap. The woman is turning her face
toward it. Her expression: not regret, but readiness. The contrast between the warm
theatrical space of the South Node past and the cool cosmic freedom of the North
Node future is the image's central tension.
A L T E R N A T E / S I M P L I F I E D V E R S I O N
Woman in lion-crown theatrical dress at stage edge, one hand extended to crowd (left),
one hand reaching toward a doorway of stars (right). Crowd in shadow, stars in cool light.
A I G E N E R A T I O N P R O M P T ( M I D J O U R N E Y / D A L L - E C O M P A T I B L E )
Victorian theatrical stage scene, woman in lion mane costume standing at stage
edge turning away from adoring crowd toward a starlit doorway, ghostly past-life
figures as translucent echoes around her, dramatic split lighting warm amber stage
vs cool starlight from doorway, dense crosshatch Victorian etching pen and ink
style, gothic theatrical atmosphere, dramatic chiaroscuro, audience in shadow,
constellation Aquarius visible through doorway, antique illustration aesthetic, black
and white --ar 6:4
Illustration 03 of 16
The Sabian Wheel

Document Location: Section 2: Sabian Symbols — placed after the introduction, before the
individual symbol descriptions
Page Position: Half-page square, centered
Dimensions: 5″ × 5″ (square)
P U R P O S E I N D O C U M E N T
Communicates the poetic and symbolic richness of the Sabian degree system; presents
the chart as an illuminated manuscript, each degree its own world.
M O O D
Scholarly — Sacred — Intricate — Medieval
L I G H T S O U R C E
Candlelight from below, as if the wheel is being studied by candlelight — warm amber
glow from center outward, illuminating the innermost glyphs most brightly and fading
toward the outer ring.
T E C H N I C A L N O T E S
The circular format demands extremely precise compass work on the outer ring divisions.
The nine medallion scenes should each be distinct but all rendered in the same fine,
miniature style — think medieval Book of Hours marginalia. The astrological symbols in
the center should be the most carefully rendered elements. Gold accent on the zodiac ring
border and on the planetary symbols at center.
F U L L A R T D I R E C T I O N P R O M P T
A circular illuminated manuscript page, styled as a medieval Book of Hours but with
astrological content replacing the religious. The outermost ring is the zodiac wheel
divided into 12 signs, each sign's symbol rendered in fine detail. Inside this, an inner
ring of nine medallion illustrations
—
each one a tiny complete scene depicting one of April's key Sabian Symbols: a
family tree with deep roots (Sun, 14
°

Virgo); a veiled woman in a garden (Moon, 7
°
Aries); a volcano erupting at night (Mercury, 17
°
Virgo); an aged philosopher with his collection of trophies (Venus, 30
°
Leo); a figure carrying bags too large for a child's frame (Saturn, 19
°
Capricorn); an ancient cathedral interior rising toward vaulted heights (Neptune, 12
°
Capricorn); holly and mistletoe arranged for winter solstice (Mars, 3
°
Gemini); a majestic mountain summit (Jupiter, 4
°
Leo). At the center of the wheel: a figure reading from an enormous open book,
surrounded by the planetary glyphs. The overall aesthetic is that of a precious,
hand-illuminated document
—
antique ink, fine detail, the sense of something both scholarly and sacred. Gold
accent on the zodiac ring border and the planetary symbols at center.
A L T E R N A T E / S I M P L I F I E D V E R S I O N
Circular zodiac wheel with 4 key Sabian Symbol miniatures at cardinal points (Sun, Moon,
Mercury, Saturn). Planetary glyphs at center. Decorative border.

A I G E N E R A T I O N P R O M P T ( M I D J O U R N E Y / D A L L - E C O M P A T I B L E )
Medieval illuminated manuscript style circular astrological wheel, zodiac signs as
decorative outer ring, nine small medallion scenes depicting Sabian Symbols
including volcanic eruption, veiled woman, family tree with roots, ancient cathedral,
child with heavy bags, philosopher with trophies, holly and mistletoe, mountain
peak, scholar reading open book at center, pen and ink crosshatch Victorian style,
warm candlelight tones, gold accent decorative border, hyper-detailed miniature
illustration style, black and white with gold --ar 1:1
Illustration 04 of 16
The Ancient Sky — Fixed Stars
Document Location: Section 3: Fixed Stars AND Appendix D: Fixed Stars Nearest Natal Points
— placed at the opening of Section 3 and as a full-width header for Appendix D
Page Position: Half-page, full width
Dimensions: 6″ × 4″
P U R P O S E I N D O C U M E N T
Establishes the ancient, cosmic scale of fixed star astrology; roots April's chart in the deep
time of stellar mythology.
M O O D
Ancient — Vast — Reverent — Crystalline
L I G H T S O U R C E
The stars themselves — specifically Spica (above left, brightest), the Galactic Center
(center horizon), and Zubenelgenubi (above right, slightly dimmer).
T E C H N I C A L N O T E S

The star rendering in this image is critical — individual stars should be rendered as fine
white dots of varying size (larger for brighter/conjunct stars), surrounded by tiny radiating
lines to suggest the scintillation of starlight. Spica should be the brightest, most formally
radiant. The Galactic Center at the horizon should be rendered as the same spiral from the
cover, but smaller and in the distance. Labels in archaic calligraphy style — slightly tilted,
written in a hand that suggests great age. Gold accent on the star labels and the Galactic
Center spiral.
F U L L A R T D I R E C T I O N P R O M P T
April stands on a high cliff at night, back to the viewer, looking up at a sky crowded
with enormous stars, each one labeled in archaic calligraphy with its name: SPICA
blazing brightest above the horizon ahead, its light falling on the cliff face where she
stands; REGULUS visible over her left shoulder, leonine and golden;
ZUBENELGENUBI directly overhead like a weight suspended on a scale, its light
more silver than gold; PROCYON to the east, quick and decided; ANTARES deep
on the horizon, red-tinged; and at the very zenith, barely visible, the Galactic Center
as a faint but unmistakable subtle spiral
—
the point around which all other stars seem to orient. The cliff face is carved with
ancient astrological markings, worn by centuries. The sky has the maximum density
of crosshatched stars. The figure is small relative to the sky
—
the scale deliberate: she is a person within a cosmos, not the other way around. Her
posture is reverent but not diminished. Gold accent on the star labels and the
Galactic Center spiral.
A L T E R N A T E / S I M P L I F I E D V E R S I O N
Silhouette of figure under labeled night sky with 4 labeled stars (Spica, Galactic Center,
Zubenelgenubi, Regulus). Stone cliff with ancient carvings.

A I G E N E R A T I O N P R O M P T ( M I D J O U R N E Y / D A L L - E C O M P A T I B L E )
Figure from behind standing on ancient stone cliff at night looking up at vast
starfield, individual stars labeled in archaic calligraphy, Spica shining brightest on
horizon, galactic center as faint spiral at zenith, Zubenelgenubi like balanced scale
overhead, Regulus over left shoulder, ancient astrological carvings in cliff face,
dense stippled crosshatch Victorian pen and ink style, dramatic night sky scale
figure small against cosmos, antique star map aesthetic, black and white with gold
star labels --ar 6:4
Illustration 05 of 16
The Five-Year-Old With the Bags — Saturn Rx H1
Document Location: Section 1: Past Lives OR the Foundational Reference section describing
Saturn Rx H1 — placed as a right-margin inset beside the Saturn Rx text
Page Position: Quarter-page inset, right margin
Dimensions: 3″ × 4″ (portrait)
P U R P O S E I N D O C U M E N T
Embodies the Sabian Symbol of Saturn at 19° Capricorn — "A Five-Year-Old Child Carrying
a Bag" — and the burden wound's earliest encoding; this small image carries enormous
emotional weight.
M O O D
Melancholy — Endurance — Premature Gravity — Quiet
L I G H T S O U R C E
Dusk light — warm but fading, coming from behind and above; the child walks toward a
darker space.

T E C H N I C A L N O T E S
This must be one of the most emotionally precise images in the set. The child should be
unmistakably small relative to the bags — the bags should be as tall as the child's waist,
stretching her arms. Her face should be turned three-quarters toward the viewer: not
crying, not complaining, simply enduring with a quality of awareness — as if she knows,
already, that this is the deal. The cobblestones should be rendered with dense
crosshatching to create a sense of weight even in the ground she walks on. The overall
image must be sympathetic, not pitying.
F U L L A R T D I R E C T I O N P R O M P T
A small child
—
approximately five years old, a girl
—
walks alone on a cobblestone street at dusk. She carries two large grocery bags,
one in each hand, each bag nearly as tall as her waist and clearly heavy
—
her arms are pulled down and slightly outward by the weight. Her face is turned
three-quarters toward the viewer: her expression is not distress but a kind of
ancient, quiet endurance
—
the face of someone who has already, at this age, understood that this is the
arrangement. Tall shadowy buildings loom on either side of the narrow street.
Above, between the rooftops, the first stars are appearing in the twilight sky
—
Saturn's rings faintly and elegantly visible in the darkening blue. The pavement is
wet from recent rain, reflecting the fading light and the first stars. The child's clothes

are simple and correct for the period
—
Victorian-adjacent but not dated. She is wearing shoes that are slightly too large,
suggesting hand-me-downs. The scene is rendered with Helquist's finest
crosshatching
—
the cobblestones dense and heavy with shadow, the child's face the lightest element
in the composition, her face always the viewer's first resting point.
A L T E R N A T E / S I M P L I F I E D V E R S I O N
Small girl seen from slightly behind carrying two large bags, first stars in twilight sky,
cobblestone street, Saturn's rings faint above.
A I G E N E R A T I O N P R O M P T ( M I D J O U R N E Y / D A L L - E C O M P A T I B L E )
Small Victorian child girl approximately five years old walking alone on wet
cobblestone street at dusk carrying two oversized grocery bags too heavy for her
small frame, expression of quiet ancient endurance on her face, tall shadowy
buildings on either side, first stars appearing in twilight sky with faint Saturn rings
visible, pen and ink crosshatch illustration, dense Victorian etching style, melancholy
atmospheric, dramatic shadow, emotional precision, Helquist style, black and white
--ar 3:4
Illustration 06 of 16

The Bucket Handle Bearer — Moon in Aries H3
Document Location: Foundational Reference section OR Introduction — placed beside the
description of the Bucket Handle chart configuration
Page Position: Quarter-page inset, right margin
Dimensions: 3″ × 4″ (portrait)
P U R P O S E I N D O C U M E N T
Visualizes the astrological concept of the Bucket Handle chart — all planets on one side,
the Moon alone on the other; communicates the structural role April's Moon plays in the
entire chart.
M O O D
Powerful — Singular — Load-Bearing — Focused
L I G H T S O U R C E
The clustered planets on the left side of the image cast their combined light; the Moon on
the right glows with its own silver-white light, separate and sovereign.
T E C H N I C A L N O T E S
This is a conceptual/symbolic illustration rather than a figurative scene. The central image
is the zodiac wheel with planets clustered in the right hemisphere as a dense field of
glyphs and circles, and the Moon alone on the left — larger, glowing, connected to the
cluster by a single bar or beam that passes through the center (the bucket handle). The
frame of the image can be the zodiac circle itself.
F U L L A R T D I R E C T I O N P R O M P T
A circular zodiac wheel rendered in the style of an antique astronomical chart. On
the right hemisphere of the wheel: nine planets clustered together
—
their symbols (Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto)
arranged in a dense, glowing constellation that occupies approximately the right 270

degrees of the circle. The cluster has a collective warmth and weight to it
—
all these forces pressing together. On the left hemisphere, alone in its 90 degrees of
sky: the Moon glyph (a crescent), rendered larger than the others and glowing with a
clear silver-white light, separated from the cluster by a sweep of empty dark space.
A single straight line
—
the bucket's handle
—
connects the Moon to the midpoint of the planetary cluster, passing through the
center of the wheel. This line is the visual axis of the entire chart. Surrounding the
wheel: fine decorative borders, constellation patterns in the margins. The empty
space between the Moon and the cluster should feel intentional
—
not vacant but significant. This is where the chart breathes.
A L T E R N A T E / S I M P L I F I E D V E R S I O N
Simple bucket shape formed by zodiac circle, nine planets as a cluster forming the bucket,
single Moon as the handle. Clean, symbolic.
A I G E N E R A T I O N P R O M P T ( M I D J O U R N E Y / D A L L - E C O M P A T I B L E )
Antique astronomical chart style circular zodiac wheel, nine astrological planet
symbols clustered in right hemisphere forming a dense bright grouping, single Moon
crescent glyph alone in left hemisphere with silver glow, a straight handle line
connecting Moon to planetary cluster through center, decorative constellation
border, Victorian pen and ink etching style, clean symbolic composition, black and

white with silver accent for Moon --ar 3:4
Illustration 07 of 16
The Stage Performer Confronts the Past
Document Location: Section 1: Past Lives — specifically beside the South Node Leo H7
paragraph
Page Position: Half-page, full width
Dimensions: 6″ × 4″
P U R P O S E I N D O C U M E N T
Shows the South Node pattern (performing for love/recognition) meeting the North Node
awakening — the moment the performer realizes she is playing a character rather than
being herself.
M O O D
Theatrical — Awakening — Theatrical Melancholy
L I G H T S O U R C E
Stage footlights below (warm amber); the wings of the stage cast cool silver from the side
— the North Node's light already entering the frame.
T E C H N I C A L N O T E S
Companion to Illustration 02 but closer in and more emotionally specific — where
Illustration 02 shows the full stage panorama, this one focuses on the performer's face
and the moment of recognition. The theatrical elements should be lush — velvet, gold
trim, an ornate proscenium — while the performer's expression is the entire story. The
viewer should feel the exact moment the mask becomes visible as a mask.
F U L L A R T D I R E C T I O N P R O M P T

Close perspective on a Victorian theatrical stage. The performer
—
a woman in full Leo regalia (golden costume, lion-mane collar, small crown)
—
stands at center stage under blazing footlights. Around her: ghostly past-life
shadows, translucent figures of previous performances
—
the bishop, the queen, the beloved teacher. She is looking directly into the wings,
where the audience cannot follow. Her expression: not sadness, but the particular
quality of recognition
—
the moment someone realizes, mid-performance, that they have been performing.
The footlights illuminate her face from below with theatrical gold. In the wings, barely

TECHNICAL PRODUCTION NOTES FOR PRINT
Paper Stock: The interior pages of the master compendium should be printed
on a cream-toned archival quality paper — ideally 100gsm uncoated stock with a
warm white or natural tone (avoid bright white, which works against the antique
ink aesthetic of Helquist-style illustration). Cream or natural stock allows the
crosshatching to read with the depth it deserves; bright white paper can make
dense pen-and-ink work feel harsh rather than rich. For the cover pages — both
the Illustration 01 full-page cover and the Illustration 16 final page — a heavier
stock is recommended: 200gsm minimum, ideally mounted on a separate weight
for the outer cover binding. The paper should have sufficient tooth for
reproduction clarity but sufficient smoothness that fine crosshatch lines are not
lost in texture.
Binding: A document of this scope and significance warrants case-bound
construction with sewn signatures rather than perfect-bind or saddle-stitch.
Sewn signatures allow the book to open fully flat at any page — essential for half-
page and full-page illustrations that must be seen in their entirety without the
gutter claiming any portion of the composition. The spine should be reinforced;
the cover boards should allow for modest embossing of the title and a small gold-
foil stamp of the key astrological symbol (the Galactic Center spiral) on the front
board.

Ink Specifications: The gold accent color should be printed as a spot Pantone
871 metallic ink rather than a CMYK approximation. CMYK gold reads as flat
yellow-brown and loses entirely the luminous, slightly raised quality of metallic
ink that makes the two-color treatment meaningful. Pantone 871 C (coated
stock) or 871 U (uncoated) provides the warm antique-gold tone that aligns with
the document's illuminated manuscript aesthetic. If the printer cannot
accommodate a spot color, the closest CMYK approximation is approximately
C:0 M:18 Y:55 K:25, but this should be considered a fallback only. The primary
black should be a rich black for full-page coverage areas and standard 100K
black for linework.
DIGITAL AND AI GENERATION GUIDANCE
For Midjourney Generation: All sixteen illustrations include Midjourney/DALL-E
compatible prompt endings as specified in each entry above. For Midjourney,
append --v 6 --q 2 to all prompts for maximum quality output. The style phrase that
most consistently achieves the Helquist-adjacent aesthetic across AI generators is:
"Victorian pen and ink etching crosshatch style, A Series of Unfortunate Events
illustration aesthetic, gothic atmospheric, dense linework, dramatic chiaroscuro,
antique illustration." This phrase should appear in every prompt and has been
included in all 16 prompts above.
For Human Illustrators Using AI as Reference: Generate a minimum of four
to six variations of each prompt before beginning any illustration. Use the AI outputs
for compositional reference — proportions, spatial relationships, value distribution,
and dramatic framing — rather than as finished art. All final linework must be hand-
drawn. The crosshatch density, the variability of pen weight, the specific quality of
deliberateness in each mark — these are what distinguish the Helquist style from

any AI approximation, and they cannot be replicated digitally. The AI generations are
maps; the hand-drawn illustrations are the territory.
Negative Prompt Guidance (for AI generation only): Include the following
exclusions in all prompts to avoid common AI drift: no color, no photorealism, no
digital painting style, no comic book style, no anime, no flat design, no gradient
fills, no soft shading, no watercolor.
